conservation.condition_narrative: Treated in 1962 with a thin coat of polyvinyl acetate (AYAF) and butyl methacrylate (Lucite #46).
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by University Art Museum, The University of New Mexico in 2025.
conservation.technical_description:
“FINE ARTS CONSERVATION LABORATORIES, INC. 
305 East 47th Street, New York 17, New York 
PLaza 3-2090 – William J. Dobbin, Director 
 
This painting has been treated at our laboratory in July 1962. It has received a final surfacing of a thin coat of polyvinyl acetate (AYAF) and butyl methacrylate (Lucite #46) 
 
A permanent record of its condition together with materials and techniques used is preserved and is available at any time. Kindly refer to our order number 1873.”

conservation.condition_narrative: "July 1962 a thin coat of polyvinyl acetate (AYAF) and butyl methacrylate lucite #46 1873" (Fine Arts Conservation Laboratories, typed label).
conservation.report_notes: Published with corresponding artwork entry in *Georgia O’Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné* (Lynes, 1999), this historical conservation information documents treatment decisions made during the artist’s lifetime. Lynes quotes information found on backing labels, and, when noted, from other sources.

other.content:
Painting is encased in a custom plexiglass box with an opening that reveals the backing. The backing has two “peeking windows” (cut outs) that showcase sections of the stretcher bars, one at the top of the piece and one in the middle left. 
 
Inscriptions and marks from upper left to bottom right: 
 
1. White sticker, labeled with “21” 
2. “…wers [rest of title obscured by label from The Downtown Gallery label 
3. The Downtown Gallery label, stamped date of “JUN 24 1963” 
4. Label from An American Place 
5. OK {5 star} (graphite) (partially covered by a label from Wadsworth Atheneum, Hartford, Conn.) 
6. “To be marked by O’Keeffe” (graphite) 
7. Fine Arts Conservation Laboratories label (July 1962) 
8. “White Black Iris” signed “O’Keeffe” 
9. UNM Art Museum label 
10. “1165 HART” (written upside down in white) 
11. “BX-13-pic” (written upside down in black) 
 
(Source: UNM Art Museum, 2025)

credit_line: University Art Museum, The University of New Mexico, Gift of the Estate of Georgia O'Keeffe [1987] (87.21.2)
description: A white lily with yellow accents stretches along the bottom third of this narrow, portrait-oriented painting. Another white lily with a green stem and leaves dominates the upper half of the frame. The abstract background fades from white at the bottom to black near the top, framing the upper lily in darkness.
